jobs.description:

About Xylem:
Xylem, Inc. is a global leader in water technology, committed to creating sustainable solutions that address the world’s most complex water challenges. We develop innovative and efficient systems that improve how water is managed, conserved, and reused—across the globe.

Position Summary:
We are hiring a Sourcing Manager. As a Sourcing Manager, you will play a pivotal role in strengthening Xylem’s supply base, optimizing total cost of ownership, and delivering materials and services that enable manufacturing excellence and long-term competitiveness. The Sourcing Program Manager is responsible for developing and executing sourcing strategies that align with business objectives and support new product introduction (NPI), cost reduction, supplier quality and capability. This role manages the end-to-end strategic sourcing lifecycle, including supplier evaluation, contract negotiation, supplier development, and performance improvement.
This individual will lead cross-functional initiatives with Engineering, Operations, Quality, and Procurement teams to ensure a best-in-class, risk-mitigated, and value-driven supply base.

Key Responsibilities:
Sourcing Strategy
- Develop and implement commodity sourcing strategies aligned with global supply chain and product roadmap objectives.
- Drive sourcing projects and ensure they are completed on time, within scope, and within
-
- Monitor industry trends and identify sourcing opportunities that support cost competitiveness and innovation.

Supplier Development
- Identify and onboard high-performing suppliers to support business growth and mitigate risk.
- Collaborate with Quality and Operations to elevate supplier capabilities and ensure alignment with Xylem’s performance standards.

Supply Base Optimization
- Rationalize and consolidate the supplier base to reduce complexity and leverage economies of scale.
- Support dual-sourcing strategies and risk mitigation plans across key commodities and regions.

Negotiations & Agreements
- Lead supplier negotiations on pricing, terms, lead times, and contracts to drive favorable commercial outcomes.
- Develop, execute, and manage supplier agreements, including long-term supply and development contracts.

Pricing Maintenance & Cost Reduction
- Provide accurate pricing data for ERP systems and ensure alignment with contracts and forecasts.
- Lead cost reduction initiatives through value engineering, volume leverage, and alternative sourcing.

Supplier Selection & Assessment
- Responsible for awarding business to qualified suppliers to meet business need in alignment with engineering, quality and supply chain strategies and policies

- Execute fair and competitive sourcing processes (RFQ/RFP) and facilitate award decisions based on TCO (Total Cost of Ownership).
- Align sourcing strategy with financial, operational and risk mitigation goals.
- Collaborate with suppliers and Category Management to ensure production capacity meets current and forecast demand.
- Lead supplier assessments, audits, and qualifications for new and existing suppliers.

Existing supplier capacity assessment
- Collaborate with suppliers and Category Management to ensure production capacity meets current and forecast demand.
- Anticipate and resolve bottlenecks or constraints that may impact delivery timelines.

Technology Roadmaps & Benchmarking
- Align supplier capabilities with product and technology roadmaps to drive innovation.
- Conduct benchmarking studies to evaluate market competitiveness of supplier pricing and services.

High-Level Expediting
- Support the procurement team in escalated material delays by driving quick-turn supplier engagement and recovery planning.
- Support Operations and Logistics on mission-critical supply continuity.

RFQ for New Parts & NPI Support
- Lead sourcing activities for new components, prototypes, and early-phase production tied to New Product Introductions (NPIs).
- Engage early with Engineering and Program Management to align sourcing plans with product timelines.

Supplier Business Reviews & Improvement
- Participate in periodic supplier business reviews focused on performance, risk, capacity, and collaboration opportunities.
- Support continuous improvement plans for underperforming suppliers and manage corrective actions.

Approved Supplier List & Preferred Part List
- Maintain and enforce compliance with the Approved Supplier List (ASL) and Preferred Part List (PPL).
- Partner with Engineering and Quality to update supplier and part approvals as needed.

Supplied Material Quality
- Work with suppliers and Quality to mitigate critical supplier quality events.
- Maintain the tooling and equipment asset management database.

Qualifications Required:
- Bachelor’s degree in supply chain, Engineering, Business, or a related field.
- 5+ years of strategic sourcing or procurement experience in a manufacturing environment.
- Experience with ERP systems (SAP preferred) and sourcing analytics tools.
- Strong contract negotiation and supplier relationship management skills.
- Solid understanding of cost modeling, value engineering, and total cost of ownership.

Preferred:
- Master’s degree or professional certifications (e.g., CPSM, CSCP, CPIM).
- Prior experience in sourcing engineered products, castings, electronics, or machined components.
- Experience supporting sustainability, compliance, and responsible sourcing initiatives.

Key Competencies:
- Strategic thinking and execution
- Strong analytical and financial acumen
- Cross-functional collaboration and influence
- Supplier engagement and development
- Problem-solving and decision-making under pressure
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

Xylem is looking for a   Senior Continuous Improvement Specialist   to help drive operational performance and Lean transformation at our   Cheektowaga manufacturing site in the Buffalo area . This is a strong opportunity for a   manufacturing engineer, industrial engineer, or continuous improvement professional   who wants to work in a visible, high-impact plant role where improvements on paper turn into measurable results on the floor.
This position supports the production of   industrial heat exchangers   serving a   rapidly growing data center market , giving the role a compelling mix of manufacturing complexity, business relevance, and long-term growth potential.
If you are energized by improving flow, increasing throughput, partnering with operations, and leading change in a real manufacturing environment, this role offers the chance to do that every day.

Why This Role Stands Out
This is not a desk-only CI role. You will spend a meaningful amount of time on the shop floor, working side by side with production teams, supervisors, and leadership to identify opportunities, solve problems, and sustain improvements. The role is ideal for someone who wants to move beyond analysis alone and directly influence how a plant performs.
You’ll have the chance to lead plant-level initiatives with visibility, ownership, and support from site leadership, while helping shape a culture of continuous improvement in a facility where hands-on engineering mindset and practical execution both matter.

What You’ll Do
In this role, you will lead cross-functional continuous improvement projects that improve   material flow, throughput, labor efficiency, and overall manufacturing performance . You’ll take projects from early-stage opportunity identification through implementation and sustainment, with a focus on driving measurable operational and financial results.
You will work closely with plant leaders and the union workforce to identify process constraints, reduce waste, improve workflow, and support better day-to-day execution across the facility. This includes helping teams address bottlenecks, strengthen standard work, and build more efficient and sustainable operating rhythms.
You’ll use   Lean, Six Sigma, and Kaizen tools   to solve complex manufacturing problems, while also using data and statistical analysis to support decisions and track results. Just as importantly, you’ll act as a change agent—building trust, gaining buy-in, and helping the site continue maturing its continuous improvement culture.
This role also offers the opportunity to coach others, share best practices, and strengthen CI capability across the organization.

What We’re Looking For
We’re looking for someone with a   Bachelor’s degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related technical field , along with   4+ years of experience in a manufacturing, industrial engineering, or continuous improvement role .
The strongest candidates will bring hands-on experience in plant environments and a track record of using   Lean, Six Sigma, and Kaizen methodologies   to improve performance. You should be comfortable using data to drive action, working across functions, and influencing both frontline teams and leadership.
This role is especially well suited for candidates who have worked in   heavy manufacturing ,   fabrication ,   industrial production , or similarly complex operational settings. Experience in a   unionized environment   is a strong plus.
We’re also looking for someone who is self-directed, pragmatic, and able to move initiatives forward with a high level of ownership. Strong communication and relationship-building skills are essential, as success in this role depends on both technical credibility and the ability to earn trust across the plant.
Preferred Qualifications
Preferred candidates may also have   Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification ,   PMP certification , or   ASQ credentials   such as   CQE   or   CMQ/OE . Experience with analytical tools such as   Minitab, JMP, or advanced Excel   is highly valued.

Work Environment
This role is   fully onsite   at our   Cheektowaga, NY facility   and requires a regular presence on the manufacturing floor. Approximately   25–50% of the role will be spent in the plant , supporting hands-on improvement efforts and collaborating directly with operations teams.

* Lead and maintain the site’s IMMEX, PROSEC, and IVA-IEPS Certification programs and other applicable foreign trade authorizations.
* Serve as the primary point of contact with customs authorities (SAT, Secretaria de Economia, and other regulatory agencies) on Trade Compliance matters.

* Own the relationship with customs brokers, freight forwarders, trade compliance consultants, Annex 24/Annex 30 providers, and other foreign trade service providers, ensuring service level compliance and continuous improvement.

* Manage Annex 24 and Annex 30, including temporary inventory control, reconciliations, discharges, expiration monitoring, and supporting documentation.
* Manage origin qualification analysis, supplier solicitation processes, USMCA certifications, and related documentation to support preferential duty treatment.

* Partner with cross-functional teams to identify risks, implement corrective actions, and continuously improve Trade Compliance processes.
* Support the effective use and integration of Annex 24 system, ERP and other compliance systems.
* Lead customs actions related to regime changes, regularizations, scrap disposition, donations, transfers, and inventory adjustments as required by Mexican foreign trade regulations.
* Conduct periodic due diligence reviews of customs brokers and external trade service providers in accordance with company compliance requirements.
* Provide functional leadership and guidance to Trade Compliance personnel and employees involved in import/export activities.
* Develop and deliver Trade Compliance training programs to employees involved in import, export, purchasing, logistics, engineering, and supply chain activities
* Report significant compliance risks, performance indicators, and improvement opportunities to site and regional leadership.

* Support denied party screening, sanctions compliance, and export control requirements in accordance with applicable regulations and company policies.
*Coordinate periodic inventory reconciliations for temporarily imported materials and fixed assets, ensuring alignment between physical inventory, ERP records, Annex 24, Annex 30, and customs records.

- Risk assessment and problem-solving.
- Continuous improvement orientation.
- Project management capability.

- Attention to detail with a strong sense of accountability.

* Strong hands-on knowledge of IMMEX, PROSEC, IVA-IEPS, Annex 24 and Annex 30.

jobs.description:

Job Summary:
Xylem is seeking a Trade Compliance Senior Analyst to support strategic trade initiatives across the enterprise. This role is focused on compliance monitoring, continuous improvement, analytics, and reporting, with responsibilities including data analysis, duty mitigation efforts, and operational process improvements. The Senior Analyst will play a critical role in advancing Xylem’s global trade compliance strategy, including driving cost savings, operational efficiencies, and risk reduction, while also helping to standardize processes, enhance visibility, and strengthen compliance oversight. As a key partner to regional and business unit teams, this individual will provide governance, reporting, and program support to ensure consistent and effective global import compliance.
This is a unique opportunity to influence global operations, broaden your trade compliance experience, and help strengthen Xylem's end-to-end trade ecosystem. Success in this role requires a self-directed problem solver who takes ownership, drives issues to resolution, and exercises sound judgment with minimal oversight. The ideal candidate proactively identifies risks and improvement opportunities, raises concerns when needed, and partners effectively with business stakeholders to develop practical, compliant solutions that support business objectives.
Key Responsibilities – Trade Compliance Senior Analyst
Program Governance & Support
- Manage and support key import compliance programs, including Xylem’s First Sale for Export program, ensuring adherence to established requirements and identifying opportunities for expansion and improvement.
- Serve as a key partner to business segments, fostering alignment between operational objectives and trade compliance requirements.
- Identify compliance risks, gaps, and emerging issues, proactively developing recommendations and driving resolution.
- Provide practical guidance to stakeholders and escalate significant compliance concerns when appropriate.
- Conduct ongoing compliance monitoring activities to assess adherence to import compliance requirements, policies, and controls.

Process Improvement & Standardization
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams to enhance trade compliance processes, systems, and reporting capabilities.
- Partner with business stakeholders to investigate findings, implement corrective actions, and strengthen compliance controls.
- Monitor program performance and recommend corrective actions and process improvements as needed.

Training & Communication
- Support the development and delivery of trade compliance training and awareness programs tailored to business and project needs.
- Communicate compliance expectations, corrective actions, and program updates in a clear and actionable manner.

Qualifications: Education, Experience, Skills, Abilities, License/Certification:
- Associate’s degree or higher

- Minimum 3 years of experience in global trade compliance, with specific expertise in customs regulations and compliance practices in North America.

- Understanding of Customs regulatory framework, including customs valuation rules, tariffs, and audit procedures.

- Good ability to identify and adapt best practices from other organizations.

- Strong writing skills.

- Self-starter with the ability to leverage efforts through effective involvement of individuals and resources from outside the immediate team.

- Positive, collegial, and collaborative approach.

Preferred Qualifications:
- US Customs Brokerage License highly desirable

- CTCS (Certified Trade Compliance Specialist) or Mexican equivalent
